title: My ordinary day
goal: Describe a daily routine and master reflexive verbs — a form English mostly does without, and which learners therefore tend to skip.
bekal: use reflexive verbs such as *mi alzo* and *mi chiamo*
string a sequence of activities together with *prima*, *poi*, *dopo*, *infine*
name everyday activities from getting up to going to bed

dialogs.title: Dialogo — Una giornata normale
dialogs.intro: Giulia describes her ordinary day. Count how many times the little word *mi* appears in front of a verb.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: What's a normal day like for you?

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.text: Mi sveglio alle sei e mezza, ma mi alzo alle sette.
lines.id: I wake up at half past six, but I get up at seven.
lines.literal: myself I-wake at-the six and half, but myself I-raise at-the seven.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Half an hour in bed? What luxury!

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.text: Poi mi lavo, mi vesto e faccio colazione.
lines.id: Then I wash, get dressed, and have breakfast.
lines.literal: then myself I-wash, myself I-dress and I-make breakfast.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: What do you eat for breakfast?

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.text: Poco: un caffè e due biscotti. Esco alle otto meno un quarto.
lines.id: Not much: a coffee and two cookies. I leave at a quarter to eight.
lines.literal: little: a coffee and two cookies. I-go-out at-the eight minus a quarter.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Vai a piedi o prendi l'autobus?
lines.id: Do you walk or take the bus?
lines.literal: you-go on feet or you-take the bus?

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.text: Vado in bici. Arrivo in ufficio alle nove.
lines.id: I go by bike. I get to the office at nine.
lines.literal: I-go in bike. I-arrive in office at-the nine.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: E il pranzo? Torni a casa?
lines.id: And lunch? Do you go home?
lines.literal: and the lunch? you-return to home?

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.text: No, mangio un panino in ufficio. Finisco alle sei.
lines.id: No, I eat a sandwich at the office. I finish at six.
lines.literal: no, I-eat a sandwich in office. I-finish at-the six.

lines.speaker: Giulia:
lines.text: La sera cucino, guardo un film e mi addormento sul divano.
lines.id: In the evening I cook, watch a movie, and fall asleep on the couch.
lines.literal: the evening I-cook, I-watch a film and myself I-put-to-sleep on-the sofa.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Ah, allora siamo uguali. Anch'io mi addormento sempre lì!
lines.id: Ah, so we're the same. I always fall asleep there too!
lines.literal: ah, then we-are equal. also-I myself I-put-to-sleep always there!

notes: **Reflexive verbs.** *Mi sveglio* literally means "I wake myself". Italian uses this form for many everyday actions that English expresses with a plain verb: wake up, wash, get dressed, shave, sit down, rest.

**The little word goes in front of the verb.** *Mi lavo*, *ti lavi*, *si lava*, *ci laviamo*, *vi lavate*, *si lavano*. It changes with the subject — don't leave *mi* in place when the subject is *tu*.
**You've been using one since Unit 1.** *Mi chiamo Budi* is a reflexive verb: "I call myself Budi". After this unit, you no longer have to learn it as a fixed phrase — it follows the pattern.

**Svegliarsi vs alzarsi.** *Svegliarsi* = your eyes open, you come to. *Alzarsi* = your body gets out of bed. English splits these too — "wake up" and "get up" — and there's often half an hour between them.
**Andare a piedi, in bici, in macchina.** Means of transport take *in*: *in macchina*, *in treno*, *in aereo*, *in bici*. Only two take *a*: *a piedi* (on foot) and *a cavallo* (on horseback).

**Fare colazione, not mangiare colazione.** You "make" breakfast rather than "eat" it, much like English "have breakfast". The same goes for *fare la doccia* (take a shower), *fare la spesa* (do the grocery shopping), *fare una passeggiata* (go for a walk). The verb *fare* covers a huge number of activities.
**Uscire and venire are irregular.** *Esco, esci, esce, usciamo, uscite, escono*. Notice how the first letter switches between *e* and *u* — learn it as it is.
**Poco means little and can stand alone.** *Mangio poco* (I don't eat much). Followed by a noun, it agrees: *poca acqua*, *pochi amici*, *poche cose*.

grammars.title: Reflexive verbs
body: The infinitive ends in *-si*: *lavarsi*, *alzarsi*, *chiamarsi*. Remove the *-si*, conjugate the verb as usual, then put the matching little word in front.
after: The *lui* and *loro* forms both use *si*. Only the verb ending tells them apart: *si lava* (one person) vs *si lavano* (several people).
To negate: *non* goes first, before the little word — *non mi alzo presto*.

Some verbs change meaning when they become reflexive: *chiamare* (to call) vs *chiamarsi* (to be called); *sentire* (to hear) vs *sentirsi* (to feel); *trovare* (to find) vs *trovarsi* (to be located).

grammars.title: Irregular verbs used in this unit
body: Three verbs that show up in almost every story about an ordinary day.
after: *Andiamo!* means "let's go!" and is probably the Italian word you'll hear most in the street. The *noi* form doubles as a "let's" invitation — no extra word needed.

sections.title: A day from waking up to going to bed

blocks.text: Notice *lavarsi i denti*: literally "to wash oneself the teeth". Italian almost never uses a possessive with body parts — not *lavarsi i miei denti*, though English says "my teeth". The reflexive little word already tells you whose teeth they are.
The first four words alone are enough to describe your whole day without sounding like a list. Mix them up; don't repeat *poi* six times.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the right reflexive word: mi, ti, si, ci, vi.
Put the verb in brackets into the right form.

items: I wake up at half past six.
Then I wash and get dressed.
I go to work by bike.
I fall asleep on the couch.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: mi — ti — si — ci — vi — si
mi alzo — esce — andiamo — vengono — ti addormenti — vi svegliate
Mi sveglio alle sei e mezza. — Poi mi lavo e mi vesto. — Faccio colazione a casa. — Vado al lavoro in bici. — La sera cucino. — Mi addormento sul divano.
Mi alzo alle sette. — Esco di casa alle otto. — Non faccio mai colazione. — Vado in ufficio in bici. — Mi addormento sul divano.
